skill.name: protocolsio-integration
skill.description: Use the protocols.io API to search, create, update, publish, and organize scientific protocols, discussions, workspaces, files, experiments, notifications, and exports.
skill.summary: Guide protocols.io API workflows for scientific protocol discovery, collaboration, documentation, and lifecycle management.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 123 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documented protocols.io URLs, illustrative HTTP requests, and ordinary API terminology. One medium semantic concern remains because permanent publication, recursive deletion, and broad exports lack explicit confirmation gates.

remediation.issue: Consequential mutations can be initiated without an explicit confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Require a fresh user confirmation showing the target and impact before publication, deletion, overwrite, or other state-changing requests.

remediation.issue: Organization exports can include files and comments by default in the example.
remediation.suggestion: Preview export scope, minimize included data, verify authorization, and obtain confirmation before requesting or downloading an organization export.

content.value_statement: Scientific teams need reliable guidance for complex protocols.io API workflows. This skill maps authentication, protocol, workspace, discussion, file, and experiment tasks to documented API operations.
actual_capabilities: Explains client token and OAuth authentication flows for protocols.io API v3.
Guides protocol search, retrieval, creation, updates, step management, publication, bookmarks, and PDF export.
Documents protocol and step discussion operations, including comments, replies, edits, and deletion.
Guides workspace access, membership requests, protocol organization, and role-based collaboration.
Covers file search, upload, download, folder organization, metadata updates, deletion, and restoration.
Describes profiles, publications, experiment records, notifications, and organization exports.
limitations: The skill provides documentation and examples, not a bundled executable API client.
Users must supply valid protocols.io credentials and have permission for each requested resource.
Endpoint availability, schemas, limits, and behavior may change with protocols.io API v3.
Publishing, deletion, upload, and export operations can create significant external side effects.

use_cases.title: Discover and compare protocols
use_cases.description: Search published protocols, retrieve steps and materials, review discussions, and collect DOI details for research planning.

use_cases.title: Organize collaborative laboratory work
use_cases.description: Manage workspace protocols, supporting files, comments, and experiment records across a laboratory team.

use_cases.title: Build a protocols.io integration
use_cases.description: Map product requirements to authentication flows, API endpoints, request parameters, rate limits, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Find a protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public protocols.io protocols about [topic]. Return the most relevant titles, DOIs, materials, and major steps. Do not change any account data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a protocol draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a new protocols.io draft for [procedure]. Define metadata, ordered steps, materials, warnings, and the API operations needed. Stop before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Design a laboratory workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a protocols.io workspace workflow for [team]. Include roles, protocol organization, file folders, comments, experiment records, and permission checks.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a production integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for integrating protocols.io with [system]. Cover OAuth, endpoint mapping, pagination, retries, validation, audit logs, and confirmation gates.

output_examples.input: Find public CRISPR protocols and summarize the best matches.
output: A ranked protocol list with titles, DOIs, publication dates, and relevance notes.
A comparison of major steps, materials, warnings, and discussion themes.
A note identifying any details that require authenticated access.

output_examples.input: Plan a new protocol and workspace structure for our microscopy team.
output: A draft protocol outline with metadata, ordered steps, expected results, and materials.
A workspace folder structure for protocols, images, raw data, analyses, and published outputs.
A review checklist that stops before creation, upload, or publication.

output_examples.input: Design a reliable protocol synchronization workflow.
output: An authentication and permission model for private and public resources.
A synchronization sequence covering pagination, version checks, rate limits, retries, and error reporting.
Confirmation requirements for publishing, deleting, uploading, and exporting data.

best_practices: Store tokens in an approved secret manager and send them only to protocols.io endpoints.
Validate identifiers, permissions, payloads, response status, and rate-limit headers for every request.
Preview changes and obtain explicit confirmation before publication, deletion, upload, or broad export.
anti_patterns: Do not place access tokens, client secrets, or private protocol data in prompts or source control.
Do not retry authentication failures or destructive requests automatically.
Do not publish, delete, upload, or export resources without showing the exact target and impact.

faq.question: Does this skill include a protocols.io client?
faq.answer: No. It provides API guidance and examples that compatible agents can adapt with approved tools.

faq.question: Which authentication methods are covered?
faq.answer: It covers client access tokens and OAuth authorization, token exchange, and refresh flows.

faq.question: Can it access private protocols?
faq.answer: Only when the supplied token and protocols.io permissions authorize access to those protocols.

faq.question: Can it publish a protocol and issue a DOI?
faq.answer: It documents the publication endpoint. Publication is permanent and public, so review and explicit confirmation are required.

faq.question: Can it manage workspace files?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents search, upload, download, metadata updates, folders, deletion, and restoration.

faq.question: How should rate limits and failures be handled?
faq.answer: Use bounded retries with exponential backoff for rate limits and server errors. Do not retry permission or validation failures automatically.
